description: Target-Fallback Bimodal Phase Selection: Step 1: Maintain two independent phase-saving arrays, `phase_focused[v]` and `phase_stable[v]`. During backtracking, update only the array corresponding to the solver's current search mode (focused/exploration vs. stable/exploitation). Step 2: Maintain a phase quality matrix `phase_score[v][2]` (tracking scores for True and False assignments). During conflict analysis, for each variable involved in the conflict, add `1.0 / LBD` to `phase_score[v][assigned_phase]`. Decay all scores by a factor of 0.95 at every restart. Step 3: Inside `kissat_decide_phase(v)`, identify the current search mode and retrieve the baseline candidate phase: `P = phase_focused[v]` if in focused mode, otherwise `P = phase_stable[v]`. Step 4: Evaluate the historical LBD quality of the candidate phase. If the opposite phase has a significantly better track record—specifically, if `phase_score[v][!P] > 1.5 * phase_score[v][P]` AND `phase_score[v][!P] > 2.0` (minimum confidence threshold)—override the baseline and select `!P`. Step 5: If the override conditions in Step 4 are not met, evaluate the absolute quality of `P`. If `phase_score[v][P] < 0.5` (indicating `P` lacks recent high-quality conflict participation), return Kissat's globally saved `target` phase (the phase from the largest conflict-free trail so far) to guide the search toward known promising global assignments; otherwise, return the baseline candidate phase `P`.

Step 4: Evaluate the historical LBD quality of the candidate phase. analysis: This variant modifies Step 5 of the original algorithm. In the original, if the override condition failed, the baseline phase P was returned blindly, even if its historical LBD score was abysmal or non-existent (stale variable). By falling back to Kissat's global 'target' phase when P's score is below 0.5, the solver leverages a globally consistent assignment for unproductive variables. This helps break out of poor local minima while retaining the bimodal LBD-driven logic for highly active variables, ultimately reducing PAR2 times by avoiding deep searches in unpromising spaces.
